errors.quote: Over $\mathbb F_2,$ norm-one tensors of indicators or coordinate units give each nonzero residual an orthonormal basis
errors.problem: The page conflates having a norm-one vector with having an orthonormal basis. In the paper, the norm-one tensors only show that each residual is nonalternating. Together with nondegeneracy (from the orthogonal decompositions), this gives an orthonormal basis through a separate argument that absorbs alternating planes. The tensors do not themselves form such a basis: for example, $t_X^\perp$ contains the alternating plane of even-weight vectors supported on $X$.
